```plato

    //==
    // # Warm starting
    //
    // Collision detection runs afresh every frame and hands the solver rows whose
    // accumulated impulses are zero. Starting from zero every frame is what makes a
    // stack of boxes sink into itself: the solver spends its whole iteration budget
    // rediscovering the support impulses it already found last frame, and never
    // gets past that.
    //
    // Warm starting copies the previous frame's accumulated impulses onto the rows
    // describing the same contact — same ordered body pair, contact point within a
    // tolerance — so the solver starts from last frame's answer and spends its
    // budget on the difference. It is the single highest-value step in a contact
    // solver, and here it is only field copying.
    //
    // The match is a linear scan per fresh row, so the cost is the product of the
    // two contact counts. A production engine keeps a persistent manifold keyed by
    // shape-feature ids and pays nothing; that bookkeeping needs a contact to have
    // an identity, which this vocabulary deliberately does not give it.

    // True when two rows describe the same contact: the same ordered body pair, and
    // contact points within `tolerance` of each other.
    SameContact(a: ContactConstraint3D, b: ContactConstraint3D, tolerance: Length): Boolean
        => a.BodyA.Value == b.BodyA.Value
        && a.BodyB.Value == b.BodyB.Value
        && a.Point.DistanceSquared(b.Point) <= tolerance.Amount * tolerance.Amount;

    // The row with new values for its three accumulated impulses and everything
    // else left alone. Rebuilt field by field: `With<Field>` accessors are
    // synthesized by the code writers, not by the language, so a Plato body that
    // wants one names the constructor.
    WithImpulses(row: ContactConstraint3D, normal: Impulse, tangent: Impulse,
        bitangent: Impulse): ContactConstraint3D
        => ContactConstraint3D(
            row.BodyA, row.BodyB, row.Point, row.Normal, row.Tangent, row.Bitangent,
            row.Penetration, row.Friction, row.Restitution, row.TargetSeparationSpeed,
            normal, tangent, bitangent);

    // The row with the three accumulated impulses of `old` copied onto it.
    WithImpulsesOf(row: ContactConstraint3D, old: ContactConstraint3D): ContactConstraint3D
        => WithImpulses(row, old.NormalImpulse, old.TangentImpulse, old.BitangentImpulse);

    // `fresh` with the accumulated impulses of the matching row in `previous`
    // copied across; a row with no match keeps its zeros. The last match wins,
    // which is immaterial because a manifold does not hold two points in one place.
    WarmStartFrom(fresh: Array<ContactConstraint3D>, previous: Array<ContactConstraint3D>,
        tolerance: Length): Array<ContactConstraint3D>
        => fresh.Map(row => previous.Reduce(row, (acc, old) =>
            SameContact(acc, old, tolerance) ? WithImpulsesOf(acc, old) : acc));

    //==
    // # Narrow phase over a whole world
    //
    // Turning a set of manifolds into the constraint rows one step solves, and one
    // worked scene — balls and a ground plane — driven end to end.
    //
    // There is NO BROAD PHASE here. The scene driver below tests every ordered pair
    // of bodies, so its cost is the square of the body count. A broad phase (a
    // sweep-and-prune over bounds, or a BVH) reduces that to the pairs whose bounds
    // actually overlap; `stdlib/geometry` already declares the spatial-index
    // vocabulary such a phase would be written against, and putting one here would
    // be a second piece of work rather than a detail of this one.

    // The rows of one manifold, with each point's approach speed measured against
    // the bodies as they currently stand — which is the moment the measurement is
    // meaningful, because the velocity solve is about to change it.
    ConstraintRows(m: ContactManifold3D, bodies: Array<SolverBody3D>, threshold: Speed)
        : Array<ContactConstraint3D>
        => m.Points.Map(p => ConstraintRow(m, p,
            SeparationSpeed(bodies[m.BodyA.Value], bodies[m.BodyB.Value], p.Position, p.Normal.Vector),
            threshold));

    // The rows of a whole set of manifolds, in manifold order. Manifolds with no
    // points contribute nothing, so a pair test that found nothing needs no
    // filtering out.
    Flatten(manifolds: Array<ContactManifold3D>, bodies: Array<SolverBody3D>, threshold: Speed)
        : Array<ContactConstraint3D>
        => manifolds.FlatMap(m => ConstraintRows(m, bodies, threshold));

    // Body `index` read as a ball: the solver body's centre, and the radius the
    // caller keeps alongside. A `SolverBody3D` carries no shape — that is what lets
    // one solver serve every shape — so a scene keeps its radii in a parallel
    // array, in body order.
    BallOf(bodies: Array<SolverBody3D>, radii: Array<Number>, index: Integer): Sphere
        => Sphere(bodies[index].Center, radii[index]);

    // Every ball-versus-ball manifold of a scene, plus every ball against one
    // ground plane. Body `groundBody` is the plane's body — an immovable
    // `SolverBody3D` — and is excluded from the ball tests.
    //
    // Ordered pairs with A's index below B's are tested, which visits each unordered
    // pair once and fixes the normal's direction: from the lower-numbered body
    // toward the higher one. The full square is enumerated and half of it discarded,
    // because an index into the upper triangle is arithmetic nobody should have to
    // read.
    BallSceneManifolds(bodies: Array<SolverBody3D>, radii: Array<Number>, ground: Plane,
        groundBody: BodyIndex, friction: Number, restitution: Proportion): Array<ContactManifold3D>
    {
        var n = bodies.Count;
        var pairs = MapRange(n * n, k => k).FlatMap(k => MaybeOne(
            k / n < k % n && k / n != groundBody.Value && k % n != groundBody.Value,
            Manifold(new BodyIndex(k / n), new BodyIndex(k % n),
                Collide(BallOf(bodies, radii, k / n), BallOf(bodies, radii, k % n)),
                friction, restitution)));
        var floors = MapRange(n, k => k).FlatMap(k => MaybeOne(
            k != groundBody.Value,
            Manifold(new BodyIndex(k), groundBody,
                Collide(BallOf(bodies, radii, k), ground), friction, restitution)));
        return pairs.Concatenate(floors);
    }

    // The constraint rows for the next step of a ball scene: detect, flatten, and
    // carry last step's accumulated impulses across. This is the whole per-frame
    // narrow phase of such a scene, and the result is what a caller puts in
    // `RigidWorld3D.Constraints` before stepping.
    BallSceneConstraints(world: RigidWorld3D, radii: Array<Number>, ground: Plane,
        groundBody: BodyIndex, friction: Number, restitution: Proportion,
        matchTolerance: Length): Array<ContactConstraint3D>
        => WarmStartFrom(
            Flatten(
                BallSceneManifolds(world.Bodies, radii, ground, groundBody, friction, restitution),
                world.Bodies,
                world.Solver.RestitutionThreshold),
            world.Constraints,
            matchTolerance);
}
```
